mn143:1.2: On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park.
mn143:2.1: Now on that occasion Anāthapiṇḍika the householder was afflicted, suffering, and gravely ill.
mn143:2.2: Then Anāthapiṇḍika the householder addressed a certain man thus:
mn143:2.3: ‘Come, good man, go to the Blessed One, and in my name pay homage with your head at his feet, and say:
mn143:2.4: “Venerable sir, Anāthapiṇḍika the householder is afflicted, suffering, and gravely ill.
mn143:2.5: He pays homage with his head at the Blessed One’s feet.”
mn143:2.6: Then go to the venerable Sāriputta, and in my name pay homage with your head at the venerable Sāriputta’s feet, and say:
mn143:2.7: “Venerable sir, Anāthapiṇḍika the householder is afflicted, suffering, and gravely ill.
mn143:2.8: He pays homage with his head at the venerable Sāriputta’s feet.”
mn143:2.10: “It would be good, venerable sir, if the venerable Sāriputta would come to the house of Anāthapiṇḍika the householder, out of compassion.”’
mn143:2.11: ‘Yes, venerable sir,’ that man replied to Anāthapiṇḍika the householder, and he went to the Blessed One, and after paying homage to him, he sat down at one side. Sitting at one side, that man said to the Blessed One:
mn143:2.12: ‘Venerable sir, Anāthapiṇḍika the householder is afflicted, suffering, and gravely ill.
mn143:2.13: He pays homage with his head at the Blessed One’s feet.’
mn143:2.14: Then he went to the venerable Sāriputta, and after paying homage to him, he sat down at one side. Sitting at one side, that man said to the venerable Sāriputta:
mn143:2.15: ‘Venerable sir, Anāthapiṇḍika the householder is afflicted, suffering, and gravely ill.
mn143:2.16: He pays homage with his head at the venerable Sāriputta’s feet;
mn143:2.18: “It would be good, venerable sir, if the venerable Sāriputta would come to the house of Anāthapiṇḍika the householder, out of compassion.”’
mn143:2.19: The venerable Sāriputta consented in silence.
mn143:3.1: Then the venerable Sāriputta dressed, and taking his bowl and outer robe, went with the venerable Ānanda as his attendant to the house of Anāthapiṇḍika the householder; having gone there, he sat down on the seat made ready. Sitting there, the venerable Sāriputta said to Anāthapiṇḍika the householder:
mn143:3.2: ‘I hope you are getting well, householder, I hope you are comfortable. I hope your painful feelings are departing and not increasing, and that their departure and not their increase, is apparent.’
mn143:4.1: ‘Venerable Sāriputta, I am not getting well, I am not comfortable. My painful feelings are increasing, not departing; their increase and not their departure is apparent.
mn143:4.2: Just as if a strong man were splitting my head open with a sharp sword, so too, venerable Sāriputta, violent winds cut through my head.
mn143:4.3: I am not getting well, venerable Sāriputta, I am not comfortable. My painful feelings are increasing, not departing; their increase and not their departure is apparent.
mn143:4.4: Just as if a strong man were tightening a tough leather strap round my head as a headband, so too, venerable Sāriputta, there are violent pains in my head.
mn143:4.5: I am not getting well, venerable Sāriputta, I am not comfortable. My painful feelings are increasing, not departing; their increase and not their departure is apparent.
mn143:4.6: Just as if a clever butcher or his apprentice were carving up an ox’s belly with a sharp carving knife, so too, venerable Sāriputta, violent winds are carving up my belly.
mn143:4.7: I am not getting well, venerable Sāriputta, I am not comfortable. My painful feelings are increasing, not departing; their increase and not their departure is apparent.
mn143:4.8: Just as if two strong men had seized a weaker man by both arms and were roasting and thoroughly scorching him over a pit of hot coals, so too, venerable Sāriputta, there is a violent burning in my body.
mn143:4.9: I am not getting well, venerable Sāriputta, I am not comfortable. My painful feelings are increasing, not departing; their increase and not their departure is apparent.’
mn143:5.2: “I will not cling to the eye, and there shall be no consciousness of mine based on the eye.”
mn143:5.5: “I will not cling to the ear, and there shall be no consciousness of mine based on the ear.”
mn143:5.8: “I will not cling to the nose, and there shall be no consciousness of mine based on the nose.”
mn143:5.11: “I will not cling to the tongue, and there shall be no consciousness of mine based on the tongue.”
mn143:5.14: “I will not cling to the body, and there shall be no consciousness of mine based on the body.”
mn143:5.17: “I will not cling to the mind, and there shall be no consciousness of mine based on the mind.”
mn143:6.2: “I will not cling to forms, and there shall be no consciousness of mine based on forms.”
mn143:6.6: I will not cling to odours …
mn143:6.7: I will not cling to flavours …
mn143:6.8: I will not cling to tangibles …
mn143:6.9: I will not cling to dhammas, and there shall be no consciousness of mine based on dhammas.”
mn143:7.2: “I will not cling to eye-consciousness, and there shall be no consciousness of mine based on eye-consciousness.”
mn143:7.6: I will not cling to nose-consciousness …
mn143:7.7: I will not cling to tongue-consciousness …
mn143:7.8: I will not cling to body-consciousness …
mn143:7.9: I will not cling to mind-consciousness, and there shall be no consciousness of mine based on mind-consciousness.”
mn143:8.2: “I will not cling to eye-contact, and there shall be no consciousness of mine based on eye-contact.”
mn143:8.6: I will not cling to nose-contact …
mn143:8.7: I will not cling to tongue-contact …
mn143:8.8: I will not cling to body-contact …
mn143:8.9: I will not cling to mind-contact, and there shall be no consciousness of mine based on mind-contact.”
mn143:9.2: “I will not cling to feeling born of eye-contact, and there shall be no consciousness of mine based on feeling born of eye-contact.”
mn143:9.5: “I will not cling to feeling born of ear-contact …
mn143:9.6: I will not cling to feeling born of nose-contact …
mn143:9.7: I will not cling to feeling born of tongue-contact …
mn143:9.8: I will not cling to feeling born of body-contact …
mn143:9.9: I will not cling to feeling born of mind-contact, and there shall be no consciousness of mine based on feeling born of mind-contact.”
mn143:10.2: “I will not cling to the earth element, and there shall be no consciousness of mine based on the earth element.”
mn143:10.5: “I will not cling to the water element …
mn143:10.6: I will not cling to the fire element …
mn143:10.7: I will not cling to the air element …
mn143:10.8: I will not cling to the space element …
mn143:10.9: I will not cling to the consciousness element, and there shall be no consciousness of mine based on the consciousness element.”
mn143:11.2: “I will not cling to form, and there shall be no consciousness of mine based on form.”
mn143:11.6: I will not cling to perception …
mn143:11.7: I will not cling to formations …
mn143:11.8: I will not cling to consciousness, and there shall be no consciousness of mine based on consciousness.”
mn143:12.2: “I will not cling to the base consisting of infinite space, and there shall be no consciousness of mine based on the base consisting of infinite space.”
mn143:12.5: “I will not cling to the base consisting of infinite consciousness …
mn143:12.6: I will not cling to the base consisting of nothingness …
mn143:12.7: I will not cling to the base consisting of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, and there shall be no consciousness of mine based on the base consisting of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.”
mn143:13.2: “I will not cling to this world, and there shall be no consciousness of mine based on this world.”
mn143:14.2: “I will not cling to the world beyond, and there shall be no consciousness of mine based on the world beyond.”
mn143:14.5: “Whatever is seen, heard, sensed, cognized, sought after, and explored by the mind, that too I will not cling to, and there shall be no consciousness of mine based on that.”
mn143:15.1: When this was said, Anāthapiṇḍika the householder wept and shed tears.
mn143:15.2: Then the venerable Ānanda said to Anāthapiṇḍika the householder:
mn143:15.3: ‘Are you foundering, householder, are you sinking?’
mn143:15.4: ‘I am not foundering, venerable Ānanda, I am not sinking.
mn143:15.5: Although I have long waited on the Teacher and on the bhikkhus worthy of esteem,
mn143:15.6: yet I have never before heard such a talk on the Dhamma.’
mn143:15.7: ‘Such talk on the Dhamma, householder, is not given to white-clothed laypeople;
mn143:15.8: such talk on the Dhamma, householder, is given to those gone forth.’
mn143:15.9: ‘Then, venerable Sāriputta, let such talk on the Dhamma be given to white-clothed laypeople as well.
mn143:15.10: For there are, venerable sir, clansmen with little dust in their eyes who are wasting away through not hearing such talk on the Dhamma;
mn143:15.11: there will be those who understand the Dhamma.’
mn143:16.1: Then, having advised Anāthapiṇḍika the householder with this advice, the venerable Sāriputta and the venerable Ānanda rose from their seats and departed.
mn143:16.2: Then, not long after the venerable Sāriputta and the venerable Ānanda had left, Anāthapiṇḍika the householder died and reappeared in the Tusita host.
mn143:17.1: Then, when the night was far advanced, Anāthapiṇḍika, a son of the gods, of surpassing beauty, having illuminated the whole of Jeta’s Grove, approached the Blessed One; having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, he stood at one side.
mn143:17.2: Standing at one side, Anāthapiṇḍika the son of the gods addressed the Blessed One in verses:
mn143:17.4: the resort of the community of seers,
mn143:17.5: dwelt in by the King of Dhamma,
mn143:17.6: a place that gives rise to joy in me.
mn143:17.8: virtue, the supreme way of life—
mn143:17.10: not by clan or by wealth.
mn143:17.12: seeing what is good for himself,
mn143:17.17: even a bhikkhu who has gone beyond
mn143:17.18: can at best only equal him.’
mn143:18.1: This is what Anāthapiṇḍika, the son of the gods, said.
mn143:18.3: Then Anāthapiṇḍika, the son of the gods, thinking:
mn143:18.4: ‘The Teacher approves of me,’ paid homage to the Blessed One, and keeping him on his right, vanished right there.
mn143:19.1: Then, when that night had passed, the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus thus:
mn143:19.2: ‘Bhikkhus, last night, when the night was far advanced, a certain son of the gods, of surpassing beauty, having illuminated the whole of Jeta’s Grove, approached me; having approached and paid homage to me, he stood at one side.
mn143:19.3: Standing at one side, that son of the gods addressed me in verses:
mn143:19.5: the resort of the community of seers,
mn143:19.6: dwelt in by the King of Dhamma,
mn143:19.7: a place that gives rise to joy in me.
mn143:19.9: virtue, the supreme way of life—
mn143:19.11: not by clan or by wealth.
mn143:19.13: seeing what is good for himself,
mn143:19.18: even a bhikkhu who has gone beyond
mn143:19.19: can at best only equal him.”
mn143:19.20: This is what that son of the gods said, bhikkhus.
mn143:19.21: Then, thinking: “The Teacher approves of me,” he paid homage to me, and keeping me on his right, vanished right there.’
mn143:20.1: When this was said, the venerable Ānanda said to the Blessed One:
mn143:20.2: ‘Surely, venerable sir, that must have been Anāthapiṇḍika, the son of the gods.
mn143:20.3: For Anāthapiṇḍika the householder had full confidence in the venerable Sāriputta.’
mn143:20.5: As far as can be reached by reasoning, Ānanda, you have reached the conclusion.
mn143:20.6: That son of the gods, Ānanda, was Anāthapiṇḍika, and no other.’
mn143:20.7: This is what the Blessed One said.
mn143:20.8: The venerable Ānanda was satisfied and delighted in the Blessed One’s words.
mn143:20.9: The Discourse Giving Advice to Anāthapiṇḍika, the first, is finished.
